approach: Find the net force on one particle from the other two and equate it to the centripetal force for its circular path of radius l/√3.

steps.text: Each pair separated by l attracts with force GM²/l²; the two forces on one particle are 60° apart, the vertex angle of the equilateral triangle, so their resultant points toward the centroid.
steps.why_this_step: The resultant of two equal vectors at angle θ has magnitude 2F cos(θ/2).

steps.text: The distance from each particle to the centroid, which is the radius of its circular path, is l/√3.
Set the net gravitational force equal to the centripetal force Mv²/r and solve for v.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the net force is twice one pair's force alone and that the particles orbit at radius l instead of the centroid distance l/√3 gives v = √(2GM/l).
Including only one of the two neighbouring forces' component toward the centroid, instead of adding both, halves the net force and gives v = √(GM/2l).
